_comment: Institutions, Paradox style. Each appears in its year (Holocene; 8800 = 1200 BC): countries knowing its origin technology embrace it at once, others see it spread (faster beside countries that have it) and embrace it for gold. Every institution a country lacks after its year makes technology cost more.

institutions.name: Iron working
institutions.description: Smiths who can work the grey metal: tools and weapons cheaper and harder than bronze.

institutions.name: The alphabet
institutions.description: A score of signs in place of hundreds: writing for merchants and soldiers, not scribes alone.

institutions.name: Coinage
institutions.description: Metal of known weight and purity, stamped by the state.

institutions.name: Philosophy
institutions.description: Reasoned inquiry into nature and the good: schools, debate and proof.

institutions.name: Paper
institutions.description: Cheap writing material: records, letters and books for the many.

institutions.name: Printing
institutions.description: Books by the thousand from a single setting of type.

institutions.name: The scientific method
institutions.description: Knowledge tested by experiment and shared in journals.

institutions.name: Industry
institutions.description: Machines driven by steam; manufactories and railways.
